This browser tool makes repeatable plate geometry. It opens in inches. A millimetre toggle remains available when a machine or material specification needs it; changing the unit converts the current values instead of changing the physical size. The downloaded SVG keeps the selected physical unit. The tool does **not** choose safe material, machine settings, joints, mounting hardware, or a final fit.

<div id="plate-builder" class="plate-builder">
<form class="plate-controls" onsubmit="return false">
<h2>Plate settings</h2>
<div class="plate-unit-control" role="group" aria-label="Measurement unit"><button type="button" data-unit-button="in" aria-pressed="true">Inches</button><button type="button" data-unit-button="mm" aria-pressed="false">Millimetres</button></div>
<div class="plate-control-section plate-fields">
<div class="plate-field plate-field--wide"><label for="pb-preset">Starting preset</label><select id="pb-preset" data-preset><option value="">Current / custom</option><option value="blank">Blank rounded plate</option><option value="mount4">Four-hole mount</option><option value="bottles6">Six-bottle row</option><option value="bottles2x3">2 × 3 bottle plate</option><option value="markers">Marker rack</option><option value="drills">Drill row</option><option value="cable">Cable plate</option></select></div>
<div class="plate-field plate-field--wide"><label for="pb-base">Base shape</label><select id="pb-base" data-key="base"><option value="rectangle">Rectangle</option><option value="rounded">Rounded rectangle</option><option value="circle">Circle</option><option value="ring">Ring</option></select></div>
<div class="plate-field"><label for="pb-width">Width / diameter (<span data-unit-symbol>in</span>)</label><input id="pb-width" data-key="width" type="number" min="1" step="0.1"></div>
<div class="plate-field"><label for="pb-height">Height (<span data-unit-symbol>in</span>)</label><input id="pb-height" data-key="height" type="number" min="1" step="0.1"></div>

</div>

<div class="plate-control-section plate-fields">

<label class="plate-check"><input data-key="autoCentre" type="checkbox"> Centre pattern first (off = top-left origin)</label>
<label class="plate-check"><input data-key="previewGuides" type="checkbox"> Show preview guides</label>

</div>
<div class="plate-actions"><button type="button" data-download>Download SVG</button><button type="button" data-json>Settings JSON</button><button type="button" data-copy>Copy share link</button><button type="button" data-reset>Reset</button></div>
</form>
<section class="plate-workspace" aria-live="polite">
<div class="plate-summary"><span>Hole diameter: <strong data-diameter></strong></span><span>Hole count: <strong data-count></strong></span><span>Units: <strong data-units>inches (in)</strong></span></div>
<div class="plate-preview" data-preview></div>
<div class="plate-status" data-status></div>

</div>

## What happens next

<div class="plate-handoff">
<div><strong>1 · Builder</strong>Set the base, measured opening, pattern and spacing. Resolve every red validation message.</div>
<div><strong>2 · Inkscape</strong>Open the SVG at 100%, confirm the document units and dimensions, then add labels, slots or project-specific geometry.</div>
<div><strong>3 · Test coupon</strong>Use the <a href="../../03-laser-cutting/04-material-fit-calibration.qmd">calibration workflow</a> to test the actual stock, machine and fit.</div>
<div><strong>4 · Onshape</strong>Use CAD when the design depends on 3D joints, motion, assemblies, toleranced interfaces or more than one plane.</div>
</div>

The [component palettes](../../03-laser-cutting/resources/index.qmd) are idea and part libraries. This builder generates repeated plate geometry. Inkscape is the 2D finishing environment. Onshape is the better tool for assemblies and 3D relationships. These are complementary workflows, not interchangeable buttons.

Need supports for the plate? Open the [Laser-Cut Leg & Support Builder](../leg-builder/index.qmd) to generate straight, angled, triangular, cross-foot or rear-easel parts with measured slots.
